doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: The 'Channel One Suite' recording and Caesar's Palace
summary: How the live album came to be recorded, the Buffalo birthday show, and Rowe's college-band memory.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

Well you know I have to ask you about the recording you made of course. Even in the Grove Dictionary of Jazz it mentions the “Channel One Suite.” And it seems like there’s been certain times in jazz history where people have recorded things, you know Illinois Jacquet with I guess “Flyin’ Home” and Coleman Hawkins “Body and Soul,”
And this particular recording, I’m interested in. Was that the only live recording done of that particular chart first of all?

No. There is a new recording that’s coming out on CD, it was live at Ronny Scott’s, it was Buddy Rich’s 50th birthday, and they’re re-issuing that. There’s also a beautiful concert hall where Benjamin Britten used to go and give his premier performances north of London called Maltings. Maltings on the Snapes. It’s like a swamp area, a bog—

Bogs and marshes, that’s what they are. But Maltings is a beautiful old concert hall, very, very experimental and a lot of flat surfaces reflecting and anyway, we did a television show there and it was recorded there. There is a studio recording of that same album of the “Mercy, Mercy” album that got shelved because we were in Buffalo, New York on my birthday in 1967 or 1968, and I remember Buddy telling me as I was playing more and more as the cadenzas got longer, he says, “Stretch out.” So in Buffalo, on my birthday, I really took it out and did a five minute cadenza in one breath, you know circular breathing and everything, and he went out front and dropped a cigarette and he said, “Oops, it’s one of those Don Menza roll your own.” This is at Kleinhan’s Music Hall, and I’m saying, oh no. And I was going to be the brunt of his jokes all night. He said, “Why didn’t you play like that on the record?” And I said, “Well you told me to play shorter.” I said, “But now that the band sounds so good, why don’t you do the record live?” He said, “Get your own band, kid,” you know, in front of 3,000 people. Well the wind up was two days later he gets on the bus and he says, “I want everyone to get your act together,” he says, “if we’re playing good now I want it even better. We’re going to do the album live at Caesar’s Palace in July.”
I was backstage when you guys did that. I was working across the street.
And we did it, and that’s the Gospel truth, that’s exactly how that — and Liberty or Pacific Jazz still has those tapes, the studio recordings of those tapes.
